title: Eli Lilly's Triple-Agonist Drug Hits 22.6% Weight Loss, Clearing Path to FDA Filing
excerpt: Retatrutide met primary endpoints in two late-stage trials of patients with obesity and diabetes or heart disease, with an FDA submission planned for early 2027.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Retatrutide achieved 22.6% weight loss in severe obesity patients over 80 weeks.
  • In type 2 diabetes patients, it resulted in 20.8% weight loss and reduced A1C by 1.6 points.
  • Eli Lilly plans FDA submission for retatrutide in early 2027, targeting multiple conditions.
  • Cardiovascular event data was inconclusive, complicating interpretation of results.

Two Trials, One Verdict

Eli Lilly on Wednesday reported positive topline results from the final two late-stage trials of retatrutide, its experimental next-generation obesity drug that targets three metabolic hormones simultaneously — GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon.

https://x.com/aftab_usa/status/2080395447508635740

In the TRIUMPH-3 trial, which enrolled 1,949 adults with severe obesity and established cardiovascular disease, patients receiving the highest weekly dose of 12 mg lost an average of 55.8 pounds — a 22.6% reduction in body weight — over 80 weeks. The TRIUMPH-2 trial, involving 1,152 patients with type 2 diabetes and obesity, showed the 12 mg dose delivered 20.8% weight loss over the same period, along with a 1.6 percentage-point reduction in A1C, a key blood sugar marker.

Both trials met their primary endpoints, according to Lilly, completing a clinical data package that now spans five positive Phase 3 studies.

"Across five positive phase 3 studies, retatrutide has shown powerful efficacy. We now have the clinical data package to support global submissions."

— Kenneth Custer, President, Lilly Cardiometabolic Health

The Cardiovascular Question

While the weight-loss numbers were strong, the cardiovascular data presented a more complicated picture. TRIUMPH-3 tracked major adverse cardiovascular events — heart attack, stroke, coronary revascularization, and death — and found 44 events across both retatrutide groups compared to 52 in the placebo cohort.

The difference was not statistically meaningful. Lilly attributed this to the fact that events "occurred less frequently than anticipated" in both arms. Reuters reported that when isolating just the three most severe events — heart attack, stroke, and death — patients on retatrutide showed a 12% higher risk than the placebo group.

BMO Capital analysts called the cardiovascular dataset "limited," making the imbalance difficult to interpret, but noted the directional benefit among patients who stayed on treatment was encouraging.

How Retatrutide Stacks Up

Retatrutide is designed to be Lilly's most potent obesity weapon. Unlike Zepbound, which activates two hormone receptors (GLP-1 and GIP), retatrutide also targets glucagon — believed to boost metabolism and increase fat burning. Novo Nordisk's competing drug Wegovy targets only GLP-1.

Earlier trials demonstrated even more dramatic weight loss: the TRIUMPH-1 study showed 28.3% reduction at 80 weeks, and TRIUMPH-4 hit 28.7% at 68 weeks. Those trials, however, did not include patients with diabetes, a population that typically sees lower weight loss on incretin drugs.

Daniel Skovronsky, Lilly's chief scientific officer, told the Wall Street Journal the treatment sets a "new benchmark" for weight loss. "At the low dose, we're seeing efficacy that's on par with other weight loss drugs at their highest doses," he said.

Side Effects and Tolerability

Gastrointestinal side effects remained the primary concern. In TRIUMPH-2, 38% of patients on the highest dose experienced nausea, 33.6% reported diarrhea, and 16.8% had constipation. Discontinuation rates due to adverse events ranged from 7.7% to 13.5% across the trials.

William Blair analysts said the tolerability profile means retatrutide will likely be directed toward patients at the higher end of the BMI spectrum, "where the benefit-risk calculus is more favorable."

What's Next

Projected Market Impact
›FDA submission planned for Q1 2027.
›Projected peak sales of $6.6 billion.
›Potential patient access by 2028.
›Lilly shares up 2% following announcement.
Market analysis and projections

Lilly plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the FDA in Q1 2027. If approved, retatrutide could reach patients by 2028. Analysts project peak sales of $6.6 billion — substantial, though modest compared to the soaring revenues of Lilly's existing obesity portfolio.

Lilly shares closed up 2% at $1,186 on Thursday. The stock has gained 10.4% in 2026, outpacing the S&P 500's 8.2% rise.
